- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after sharp historical spikes, then overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model holds prices too high for extended periods after peaks.
- Model exhibits lag in adjusting to recent downward trends; often fails to reduce forecast after a drop in history.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in the latter half of the 30d window, even when true values are declining.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent low values; underestimates the extent of correction needed.
- Overshoots after spikes, then fails to smoothly decay — often overcorrects downward too early or too late.
- Forecasts are generally too optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and too pessimistic in the long term (last 10–20 days).
